recipes.name: Rinderbrühe (Beef Stock)
recipes.flavorProfile: A clear, golden, deeply beefy broth with a sweet note from the charred onion and a gentle warmth of clove and pepper.
recipes.healthBenefit: A light broth that carries some protein and gelatin from the shin and bones and minerals from the root vegetables, salted lightly so the dish it goes into sets the seasoning.

ingredients.prepNote: 1000 g beef marrow and soup bones simmered in 3500 ml water, counted as 3500 g home-made beef stock (1 g per ml); the bones themselves are not eaten

ingredients.cutPrep: halved, unpeeled, the cut sides charred dark in a dry pan

ingredients.prepNote: the source salts at the end with no amount

instructions: Rinse the bones, put them with the shin in a large pot, cover with the cold water and bring slowly to a simmer, 30 to 40 minutes.
Skim off the grey foam as it rises, then keep at a bare simmer, uncovered, for 1 hour.
Add the charred onion, carrot, celeriac, leek, parsley root and parsley stalks, the cloves and peppercorns.
Simmer gently for 2 to 2.5 hours more, never at a rolling boil, so the broth stays clear.
Lift out the meat (it is good sliced and eaten with horseradish, or cut into a soup) and strain the broth through a cloth-lined sieve.
Salt lightly, cool quickly, and lift off the fat once it sets. Makes about 2.5 litres; keeps 3 to 4 days chilled or 3 months frozen.

nutritionHighlights.note: A little protein and gelatin from the shin and the bones.
Drawn out of the carrot, celeriac and leek.

recipes.curationNote: Wikibooks Kochbuch, Fleischbrühe for every amount and step; 750 g to 1 kg soup beef, soup bones, onion, carrots, celeriac, half a leek, parsley and parsley root, about a dozen peppercorns, 2 to 3 cloves, salt at the end.

recipes.name: Hühnerbrühe (Chicken Stock)
recipes.flavorProfile: A pale golden, rich chicken broth with soft sweetness from the root vegetables and a fine layer of chicken fat.
recipes.healthBenefit: A light, warming broth with some protein and gelatin from a whole boiling hen and minerals from the vegetables.

ingredients.cutPrep: halved, cut sides browned in a dry pan

instructions: Put the hen in a large pot, cover with the cold water and bring slowly to a simmer, skimming the foam, about 30 minutes.
Add the onion, carrot, celeriac, leek, parsley stalks, cloves and peppercorns.
Simmer very gently, half covered, for 1.5 to 2 hours, until the meat falls from the bones.
Lift out the hen and pick the meat for Hühnerfrikassee or a soup.
Strain the broth, salt lightly and chill. Skim the fat when set, or keep a little for flavor. Makes about 2.5 litres; keeps 3 days chilled.
recipes.curationNote: Wikibooks Kochbuch, Hühnerbrühe for every amount and step; one 1.5 kg hen like ours; salt to taste.

recipes.name: Gemüsebrühe (Vegetable Stock)
recipes.flavorProfile: A savory, sweet-rooted broth with the toasty edge of charred onion and a little spice from allspice and clove.
recipes.healthBenefit: A plant-only broth that carries potassium and a little of the vitamins from the root vegetables, with no meat or dairy.

ingredients.cutPrep: 2 onions, halved, cut sides charred in a dry pan

instructions: Char the cut sides of the onions in a dry heavy pan until nearly black.
Heat the oil in a large pot and sweat the carrot, celeriac and leek for 5 to 8 minutes without browning.
Add the onions, parsley, bay, cloves, allspice and peppercorns, pour in the cold water and bring to a simmer.
Simmer gently, half covered, for 45 to 60 minutes.
Strain, pressing lightly on the vegetables, and season with the salt. Makes about 2 litres; keeps 4 days chilled.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the carrots, celeriac and leek.

recipes.curationNote: Wikibooks Kochbuch, Gemüsebrühe for every amount and step; same vegetables, herbs and spices; Wikibooks gives counts, not weights, and salt to taste.

recipes.name: Fischfond (Fish Stock)
recipes.flavorProfile: A light, clean, faintly briny stock with a soft aroma of leek, celery and bay, and a gentle warmth from white pepper and coriander seed.
recipes.healthBenefit: A light stock that brings a little protein and minerals from white fish bones into sauces and soups.

ingredients.prepNote: 1000 g white fish bones and heads (plaice, cod, sole), gills removed simmered in 1500 ml water, counted as 1500 g home-made fish stock (1 g per ml); the bones themselves are not eaten

ingredients.cutPrep: stalks, the herb stalks the source adds to the vegetables
1 1/2 large cloves, in their skins, lightly crushed

instructions: Soak about 900 g of fish frames with heads in cold water for 15 minutes, then rinse them well.
Dice the vegetables about 1 cm and lightly crush the garlic.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot and sweat the vegetables, garlic, parsley stalks, peppercorns, coriander seed and bay leaves until glassy, without browning.
Add the fish frames and cover generously with cold water, about 1.5 litres. Bring to the boil, then turn the heat right down and simmer very gently for about 20 minutes, skimming off the foam often.
Strain through a fine sieve or a cloth. Keep chilled in clean jars.

nutritionHighlights.note: A little, from the fish bones and heads.

recipes.curationNote: Stay Spiced (Roland Trettl), Fischfond for every amount and step; serves 4, scaled to our 6 (x1.5): 600 g fish frames with heads, 200 g white vegetables (fennel, celery, onion, leek, a few herb stalks), 1 tsp white peppercorns, 1 large garlic clove in its skin, 1/2 tsp coriander seed, 2 bay leaves, 3 tbsp olive oil; covered generously with cold water, no amount given; simmered about 20 minutes.

recipes.name: Bratensoße (Brown Gravy)
recipes.flavorProfile: A dark, glossy, deeply roasted gravy with red wine depth and herbal notes, the sauce poured over a Sunday roast.
recipes.healthBenefit: A rich sauce used in small amounts, carrying flavor and a little gelatin from roasted bones.

ingredients.prepNote: 1000 g pork or veal bones, chopped small simmered in 400 ml water, counted as 400 g home-made beef stock (1 g per ml); the bones themselves are not eaten

ingredients.cutPrep: a quarter bulb, peeled, roughly diced
1 tbsp, mixed with a little cold water, only if needed

instructions: Chop the bones. Heat the oil in a large pot over high heat and brown the bones well. Add the vegetables and brown them, stirring.
Pour off the fat, stir in the tomato paste and roast it briefly.
Pour in a third of the wine, scrape up the browned bits and let it boil away completely. Repeat with the second and last thirds.
Cover with the broth and add the bay leaf, pepper, thyme sprigs and garlic. Simmer about 2 hours, then strain through a cloth-lined sieve.
Reduce the stock to a full-flavored sauce, about 600 ml, and season with salt. If it is too thin, whisk in the cornstarch slurry and simmer 1 minute.

nutritionHighlights.note: A little gelatin and protein from the roasted bones.

recipes.curationNote: Lecker, Bratensoße selber machen for every amount and step; 1 kg bones browned in 2 tbsp oil with 1 carrot, a quarter celeriac and 1 onion; 1 tbsp tomato paste; 200 ml red wine added in thirds; 1 l lightly salted broth; spices to taste (allspice, juniper, pepper, bay, star anise given as examples); 2 garlic cloves halved in their skins; half a bunch of thyme; salt; 1 tbsp cornstarch if needed; simmered about 2 hours, strained and reduced.

recipes.name: Rahmsoße (Cream Sauce)
recipes.flavorProfile: A smooth, pale rosy cream sauce, mild and savory, the classic Rahmsoße for schnitzel and Spätzle.
recipes.healthBenefit: A rich sauce for small portions that brings a little calcium and vitamin A from the cream and butter.
instructions: Melt the butter in a small pan, stir in the flour and cook for 1 to 2 minutes without letting it brown.
Stir in the tomato paste for a few seconds.
Pour in the hot stock a little at a time, whisking after each addition so no lumps form.
Whisk in the cream and simmer gently for about 5 minutes, stirring, until it coats a spoon.
Season with salt and pepper.
recipes.curationNote: Gaumenfreundin, Rahmsoße selber machen for every amount and step; 30 g butter, 30 g flour, 1 tbsp tomato paste, 400 ml beef stock, 200 g cream, salt and pepper to taste, for 4; scaled to our 250 ml of stock.

recipes.name: Jägersoße (Mushroom Sauce)
recipes.flavorProfile: A creamy, earthy mushroom sauce with soft onion, a little tomato paste and beef stock, made for Jägerschnitzel.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mushrooms bring B vitamins and potassium to a rich sauce best eaten in modest portions.
instructions: Melt the butter in a wide pan and soften the onion for 2 to 3 minutes.
Raise the heat, add the mushrooms and fry until their liquid has cooked away and they color, 6 to 8 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and dust over the flour, stirring for 1 minute.
Pour in 300 ml of the beef stock a little at a time, stirring, and simmer 5 minutes.
Stir in the cream and simmer 3 to 5 minutes more, until creamy. Season with the salt and pepper.

nutritionHighlights.note: Riboflavin and niacin from the mushrooms.

recipes.curationNote: Gaumenfreundin, Jägersoße selber machen for every amount and step; serves 4 like ours; salt and pepper to taste.

recipes.name: Frankfurter Grüne Soße
recipes.flavorProfile: A cool, bright green herb sauce, tangy with yoghurt and sour cream, grassy from seven fresh herbs and rich with chopped egg.
recipes.healthBenefit: A large handful of fresh herbs brings vitamin K, vitamin C and folate, with protein and calcium from the eggs and cultured dairy.
instructions: Wash the herbs, spin them dry and pick off the coarse stalks.
Chop the herbs very finely by hand or in a food processor in short pulses; they should stay green and not turn to mush.
Stir the sour cream and yoghurt together with the vinegar and mustard until smooth.
Chop 4 of the eggs finely and stir them in with the herbs. Season with salt and pepper.
Chill for at least 1 hour so the herbs flavor the sauce. Serve cold, with the last 2 eggs halved on top, beside boiled potatoes.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the parsley, chives, cress and borage.
From the yoghurt and sour cream.

recipes.curationNote: Wikibooks Kochbuch, Grüne Sauce for every amount and step; 400 g sour cream and 500 g yoghurt like ours; salt and pepper to taste.

recipes.name: Meerrettichsoße (Horseradish Sauce)
recipes.flavorProfile: A warm, creamy, gently sharp sauce with the nose-tingling heat of horseradish softened by broth and a little cream.
recipes.healthBenefit: Horseradish brings its sharp glucosinolate compounds and a little vitamin C to a light white sauce.
instructions: Melt the butter in a saucepan, scatter in the flour and cook it until golden.
Pour in the strained hot broth, stirring so no lumps form.
Stir in the cream and horseradish and leave it 5 minutes over low heat.
Season with salt and pepper. Serve with boiled beef.

nutritionHighlights.note: The sharp compounds in fresh horseradish.

citations.source: EAT SMARTER, Tafelspitz mit Meerrettichsoße und Kartoffeln

recipes.curationNote: EAT SMARTER, Tafelspitz mit Meerrettichsoße und Kartoffeln for every amount and step; serves 4, doubled to our 8: the sauce is 2 tbsp butter, 1 tbsp wholemeal spelt flour browned golden, 400 ml strained beef broth, 1 tbsp horseradish, 1 tbsp whipping cream, left 5 minutes; salt and pepper to taste.

recipes.name: Spätzleteig (Spätzle Batter)
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, chewy, eggy little noodles with an irregular, rustic shape that soaks up gravy and melted butter.
recipes.healthBenefit: A filling egg and wheat noodle that brings protein from the eggs and carbohydrate from the flour.

ingredients.cutPrep: 1 tsp, plus more for the cooking water

instructions: Stir the flour, semolina and salt in a bowl, then add the eggs.
Beat with a wooden spoon for 5 to 10 minutes until the batter is smooth, thick and throws bubbles; it should drop slowly from the spoon.
Rest the batter for 10 to 15 minutes while a large pot of salted water comes to a gentle boil.
Scrape the batter in thin strips off a wet board into the water, or press it through a Spätzle press, working in batches.
When the Spätzle float, after 1 to 2 minutes, lift them out with a slotted spoon into a bowl of warm water or straight onto a warm dish.
Serve tossed in a little butter, or use as a dish calls for. Serves 4 as a side.
recipes.curationNote: Wikibooks Kochbuch, Spätzle for every amount and step; 300 g flour, 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp semolina, 4 eggs for 4 servings, same as ours.

recipes.name: Nudelteig (Egg Noodle Dough)
recipes.flavorProfile: A silky, golden egg pasta with a firm bite, rolled thin for soup noodles or cut wide for Bandnudeln.
recipes.healthBenefit: Fresh egg noodles bring protein from the eggs alongside the wheat.
instructions: Mix the flour, semolina and salt on a board and make a well in the middle.
Break in the eggs, add the oil, and work them into the flour with a fork, then knead by hand for 8 to 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Wrap and rest for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Roll out very thin with a pin or a pasta machine, dust with semolina and cut into noodles as the dish needs.
Cook in plenty of salted boiling water for 2 to 4 minutes, until just tender.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the eggs and durum semolina.

recipes.curationNote: Wikibooks Kochbuch, Eiernudelteig for every amount and step; 100 g flour, 100 g durum, 2 eggs, 1 tsp olive oil, salt; scaled by 1.5 to our 300 g of flour.

recipes.name: Hefeteig (Sweet Yeast Dough)
recipes.flavorProfile: A soft, light, faintly sweet and buttery dough, the base of Hefezopf, Streuselkuchen and Dampfnudeln.
recipes.healthBenefit: An everyday sweet bread dough that brings carbohydrate with a little protein from the milk; a treat rather than a staple.

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

instructions: Crumble the yeast into the lukewarm milk with 1 teaspoon of the sugar and stir until dissolved; leave 10 minutes until foamy.
Put the flour in a bowl with the rest of the sugar and a pinch of salt. Add the yeast milk and the soft butter.
Knead for 8 to 10 minutes by hand or 5 minutes in a mixer until smooth, silky and pulling away from the bowl.
Cover and leave in a warm place for 1 to 1.5 hours, until doubled.
Knock back, shape as the recipe needs (a braid, a sheet for a tray cake, rolls) and let it rise 20 to 30 minutes more before baking. A braid bakes 25 to 35 minutes at 350°F (180°C).

nutritionHighlights.note: From the wheat flour and sugar.

recipes.curationNote: Wikibooks Kochbuch, Hefeteig for every amount and step; 500 g flour like ours.

recipes.name: Mürbeteig (Shortcrust)
recipes.flavorProfile: A crisp, buttery sweet pastry made with wholemeal flour and whole cane sugar, the base for German tarts.
recipes.healthBenefit: A rich butter pastry, a treat in small slices, carrying vitamin A from the butter and egg.
instructions: Put the sugar, egg and butter in a bowl and add the flour, baking powder and salt.
Mix on low speed with a hand mixer until the dough is smooth.
Roll out two thirds of the dough and press it into the base of a greased springform tin; line the sides with the rest.
Prick the base and sides several times. Bake in a preheated oven at 390°F (200°C) about 30 minutes, or fill and bake as the tart recipe says.
recipes.curationNote: EAT SMARTER, Grundrezept für Mürbeteig-Tortenboden (closest published version) for every amount and step; no free 1-2-3 Mürbeteig with yolks, vanilla and lemon could be opened; this tart base serves 12 like ours: 100 g whole cane sugar, 1 egg, 125 g butter, 250 g wholemeal flour, a knife tip of baking powder, a pinch of salt; lines a springform; 200°C about 30 minutes.

recipes.name: Quark-Öl-Teig
recipes.flavorProfile: A soft, tender, quickly made dough with a light tang from the quark, between a scone and a yeast dough.
recipes.healthBenefit: Quark adds protein and calcium to a quick dough, which is lower in fat than a butter pastry.

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

ingredients.cutPrep: for a sweet dough; leave out for savory

instructions: Stir the quark, oil, milk, egg and sugar together until smooth.
Mix the flour with the baking powder and add half of it, stirring.
Knead in the rest of the flour by hand to a smooth, soft dough that no longer sticks; add a spoon of flour if needed.
Roll out straight away, without resting, onto a baking tray for a fruit tray cake, or cut and shape into rolls.
Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 20 to 35 minutes depending on the topping and size, until golden underneath.
recipes.curationNote: Lecker, Quark-Öl-Teig Grundrezept for every amount and step; 300 g flour, 1 packet baking powder, 150 g quark, 6 tbsp milk, 1 egg, 6 tbsp oil; 2 tbsp sugar sweet or a pinch of salt savory.

recipes.name: Roggensauerteig (Rye Sourdough Starter)
recipes.flavorProfile: A thick, grey-brown paste that smells sour, fruity and a little like beer, which gives German rye bread its tang.
recipes.healthBenefit: A live culture of lactic acid bacteria and wild yeast whose long fermentation makes rye bread easier to digest and helps free minerals from the grain.
instructions: Day 1: stir 50 g rye flour with 50 ml lukewarm water in a clean jar, cover loosely and keep somewhere warm, 77 to 86°F (25 to 30°C).
Days 2 to 5: once a day, stir in another 50 g rye flour and 50 ml lukewarm water.
By day 4 or 5 it should be bubbly, risen and pleasantly sour. If it smells of nail varnish, feed it twice a day for a day.
On baking day take what the recipe needs and keep about 50 g back as Anstellgut in the fridge for the next bake.
To refresh, mix 1 part Anstellgut with 10 parts rye flour and 10 parts water and leave 12 to 18 hours at room temperature. Makes about 500 g.

nutritionHighlights.note: Live cultures that sour and raise the dough.

recipes.curationNote: Lecker, Sauerteig selber machen for every amount and step; 50 g rye flour type 1150 and 50 ml lukewarm water a day for 5 days, about 500 g.

recipes.name: Laugenteig (Pretzel Dough)
recipes.flavorProfile: A chewy, dense bread with a deep mahogany, glossy crust and the unmistakable salty, alkaline bite of a Laugenbrezel.
recipes.healthBenefit: A plain wheat bread that brings carbohydrate and a little protein; the coarse salt on top makes it a salty food to enjoy in moderation.

ingredients.name: food-grade lye (sodium hydroxide), for a 4% bath
ingredients.cutPrep: dissolved in 1 litre cold water; or 3 tbsp baking soda boiled in 1 litre water

instructions: Dissolve the yeast and sugar in the lukewarm water. Knead with the flour, salt and butter for 8 to 10 minutes to a firm, smooth dough.
Rest 15 minutes covered, then divide into 8 pieces and roll each into a rope 50 to 60 cm long, thick in the middle and thin at the ends.
Twist into pretzels, lay them on a floured cloth and leave uncovered in the fridge for 1 hour, so a skin forms.

Wearing gloves and goggles, stir the lye into the cold water in a glass or steel bowl. Dip each pretzel for 10 to 15 seconds, lift onto a tray lined with baking paper. With baking soda instead, dip them for 30 seconds in the gently boiling soda water.
Sprinkle with coarse salt, cut the thick belly once with a sharp knife, and bake at 400°F (200°C) for 15 to 20 minutes until deep brown. Makes 8 pretzels.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the coarse salt on top.

recipes.curationNote: t-online, Wie macht man Laugengebäck (Laugenbrezeln) for every amount and step; 500 g flour like ours (source shapes 12, we shape 8 larger).

recipes.name: Gewürzgurken (Pickled Cucumbers)
recipes.flavorProfile: Crunchy, sweet-sour small cucumbers fragrant with dill, mustard seed and bay, the pickle served beside cold cuts and in Rouladen.
recipes.healthBenefit: A low-calorie pickle that adds flavor and a little vitamin K; it carries salt and sugar, so a couple at a time.

ingredients.cutPrep: small pickling cucumbers, scrubbed, ends trimmed

instructions: The day before, dissolve 100 g salt in enough cold water to cover the cucumbers and leave them in it overnight. Rinse them well and pat dry; that salt is poured away and not counted.
Pack the cucumbers upright in clean jars with the shallot rings, dill, tarragon, bay leaves, mustard seed and peppercorns.
Bring the white wine vinegar, water and sugar to the boil and pour it over the cucumbers so they are covered; close the jars.
Set the jars in a pan or oven and heat them at 176°F (80°C) for 30 minutes so they keep, then leave to cool.
Wait at least 2 weeks before eating. Unopened jars keep 6 to 9 months in a cool, dark place; open ones 4 weeks in the fridge.

citations.source: Lecker, Gurken einlegen nach Omas Rezept

recipes.curationNote: Lecker, Gurken einlegen nach Omas Rezept for every amount and step; 2 kg cucumbers like ours.

recipes.name: Süßer Senf (Bavarian Sweet Mustard)
recipes.flavorProfile: A coarse, dark, caramel-sweet mustard with only a gentle heat, made for Weißwurst and Leberkäse.
recipes.healthBenefit: A condiment with a little mineral content from the mustard seed; sweet, so eaten by the spoonful.

ingredients.cutPrep: brown seed, frozen 1 hour, then coarsely ground

instructions: Freeze the yellow and brown mustard seed for about 1 hour, then grind coarsely in a mill or mortar.
Bring the water to the boil with the bay leaf, pour it over the ground seed and leave 10 minutes. Let it cool and take out the bay leaf.
Caramelise the brown sugar in a pan until golden.
Stir the caramel, honey, vinegar, tarragon and salt into the mustard.
Whisk every 5 to 6 minutes until the mixture is even.
Spoon into clean jars, close tightly and leave about 3 days in the fridge. Keeps 6 to 8 weeks cool and dark.

nutritionHighlights.note: A little, from the mustard seed.

recipes.curationNote: Lecker, Süßer Senf mit Estragon for every amount and step; makes about 480 ml, scaled to our 20 tbsp (x0.625): 120 g yellow and 70 g brown mustard seed, frozen 1 hour and coarsely ground; 150 ml water boiled with 1 bay leaf and poured over; 100 g brown sugar caramelised; 3 tsp honey, 100 ml white wine vinegar, 1 tsp dried tarragon, a pinch of salt; 3 days in the fridge.

recipes.name: Quark
recipes.flavorProfile: A fresh, mild, gently tangy curd cheese, smooth and spoonable, used in cheesecake, dips and doughs.
recipes.healthBenefit: A cultured fresh cheese rich in protein and calcium, with live cultures from the buttermilk.

ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

instructions: Stir the buttermilk into the milk in a clean pot or bowl, cover and leave at warm room temperature for about 2 days, until thick and set like yoghurt.
Set the covered pot in an oven at 86 to 95°F (30 to 35°C) for about 2 hours so the whey separates from the curd.
Line a sieve with a clean cloth, pour in the curd and let it drain for 2 hours, or longer for a firmer quark.
Stir until smooth and keep it in a closed jar in the fridge. Makes about 500 g; keeps 5 days.

nutritionHighlights.note: Concentrated in the curd as the whey drains off.

recipes.curationNote: Utopia, Quark selber machen for every amount and step; 1 litre milk and 80 ml buttermilk, about 250 g quark; doubled to our 2 litres.

recipes.name: Griebenschmalz
recipes.flavorProfile: A rich, savory spreading lard full of crisp pork cracklings and bacon, sweet fried onion and apple, with thyme and a hint of juniper and clove, spread thick on rye bread.
recipes.healthBenefit: A very rich fat spread, a treat in thin layers, which carries some vitamin D from the pork fat.

ingredients.cutPrep: small tart apples, peeled and finely diced
1 whole clove, lifted out after rendering

ingredients.baseName: Pork breakfast bacon, raw cured, smoked

instructions: Finely dice the leaf fat and the pork belly.
Render the diced fat slowly in a large pot with the clove and juniper berries until glassy, then lift the spices out.
Peel and finely chop the onions; peel and finely dice the apples.
When the cracklings turn golden, add the apples and onions.
When the fat starts to brown, add the thyme and stir often.
Fry the bacon crisp in a separate pan, crumble it and stir it into the fat.
Pour into clean jars, let cool, close tightly and keep chilled; it keeps about 2 to 3 weeks.

nutritionHighlights.note: Mostly monounsaturated and saturated fat from the pork leaf fat and belly.

citations.source: EAT SMARTER, Schmalz mit Thymian, Grieben, Apfel und Speck

recipes.curationNote: EAT SMARTER, Schmalz mit Thymian, Grieben, Apfel und Speck for every amount and step; halved to match our 500 g of fat: 500 g pork leaf fat (Flomen), 500 g fatty pork belly, 2 cloves, 4 juniper berries, 4 onions, 4 small tart apples, 3 rashers of breakfast bacon, 1 tsp dried thyme; no salt, pepper, marjoram, garlic or caraway.

recipes.name: Butterschmalz (Clarified Butter)
recipes.flavorProfile: A pure golden cooking fat with a nutty, toasty butter taste that can be heated high without burning.
recipes.healthBenefit: A concentrated butterfat for frying; it carries vitamin A and is nearly free of lactose once the milk solids are strained off.
instructions: Melt the butter in a heavy saucepan over low heat.
Let it simmer very gently for 20 to 30 minutes; the white foam rises and the milk solids sink and turn golden.
Skim off the foam, and take it off the heat when the bubbling quietens and it smells of hazelnut.
Strain through a sieve lined with kitchen paper or a cloth into a clean jar, leaving the solids behind.
Close once cool. Makes about 400 g; keeps for months in the fridge.
recipes.curationNote: Wikibooks Butterschmalz (500 g butter, simmered gently about 30 minutes until the foam subsides and the solids turn golden, strained through paper). Only one source opened for this one; the method is the standard clarified butter technique.

recipes.name: Apfelmus
recipes.flavorProfile: A soft, fresh and tart apple purée with a little sweetness and cinnamon, served with Reibekuchen, Kartoffelpuffer and Milchreis.
recipes.healthBenefit: Cooked apples bring fiber, including pectin, and a little vitamin C, with only a small amount of added sugar.

ingredients.cutPrep: tart apples (Boskop, Elstar), peeled, cored and cut in pieces

instructions: Toss the apple pieces with the lemon juice in a pot.
Add the apple juice, sugar and butter, cover and simmer over low to medium heat for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until the apples fall apart.
Mash with a potato masher for a chunky Apfelmus or purée it for a smooth one.
Stir in the cinnamon and taste; add a little more sugar only if the apples were very sour.
Serve warm or cold. Keeps 5 days in the fridge, or a year in jars heated 30 minutes at 194°F (90°C).

nutritionHighlights.note: A little, from the apples and lemon.

citations.source: Emmi kocht einfach, Apfelmus selber machen

recipes.curationNote: Emmi kocht einfach, Apfelmus selber machen for every amount and step; 1 kg apples, same batch as ours.

recipes.name: Pflaumenmus
recipes.flavorProfile: A thick, dark, almost black plum butter, deeply fruity and spiced with cinnamon and clove, for Buchteln, Germknödel and bread.
recipes.healthBenefit: Long-cooked plums keep their fiber and potassium; it is sweetened, so a spoonful at a time.

ingredients.cutPrep: optional, stirred in at the end

instructions: Mix the plums with the sugar, vanilla sugar, cinnamon sticks and cloves in a deep roasting tin and leave covered overnight so the juice runs.
Put the tin in the oven at 320°F (160°C), uncovered, and cook for about 3 hours, stirring every 30 to 45 minutes.
Cook until thick and dark brown and a spoon drawn through leaves a clear track; it can take up to 4.5 hours.
Remove the cinnamon and cloves, purée if you want it smooth, and stir in the rum if using.
Fill boiling hot into clean jars, close and turn upside down for 5 minutes. Makes about 5 jars of 300 g; keeps a year unopened.
recipes.curationNote: Küche gemacht, Pflaumenmus im Backofen for every amount and step; 2.5 kg plums, 400 g sugar, 2 cinnamon sticks, 2 packets vanilla sugar, 3 to 4 cloves, same size as ours; rum from Lecker (3 tbsp for 3.5 kg).

recipes.name: Geriebener Meerrettich (Prepared Horseradish)
recipes.flavorProfile: A sharp, clean, sinus-clearing grated horseradish with a little vinegar sourness, served with Tafelspitz, ham and fish.
recipes.healthBenefit: Fresh horseradish carries its sharp glucosinolate compounds and some vitamin C, eaten in small amounts.

ingredients.cutPrep: root, peeled and very finely grated

instructions: Peel the horseradish root and grate it finely, by an open window or wearing glasses; the vapours sting.
Stir in the salt and sugar straight away.
Pour over the vinegar and water at once, which stops the root turning brown and holds its sharpness.
Pack into small clean jars so the horseradish is covered with liquid, and close.
Keep in the fridge, or cool and dark; it keeps up to 3 months. Stir a spoon into cream or sauces as needed.

nutritionHighlights.note: The sharp compounds that give horseradish its bite.

recipes.curationNote: Gartenjournal (200 g root finely grated, salt, a little sugar, covered with vinegar in sterile jars, keeps 3 months) and Utopia (grate, cover with salt and vinegar) agree.

recipes.name: Weinkraut (Sauerkraut Braised in Wine)

recipes.name: Kartoffelsuppe

recipes.name: Erbsensuppe

recipes.name: Linseneintopf
recipes.flavorProfile: Hearty and earthy, with soft lentils, smoked pork and sausage, sharpened at the end with a splash of vinegar.

recipes.name: Gulaschsuppe

recipes.name: Sauerbraten

recipes.name: Frikadellen
recipes.flavorProfile: Juicy, well-browned patties of beef and pork, soft inside from soaked roll, with sweet onion, parsley and a little paprika.
recipes.healthBenefit: The meat gives protein, iron, zinc and vitamin B12; pan-fried, they are good hot or cold with mustard and a potato salad.

components.note: 1 each, stale, soaked in water and squeezed

instructions: Soften the onion in the butter over low heat, 3 to 4 minutes, and let it cool a little.
Mix the minces with the squeezed roll, onion, eggs, paprika, salt, pepper and parsley until it holds together.
Shape 8 flat patties with wet hands.
Fry them in the hot oil over medium heat, 5 to 6 minutes a side, until well browned and cooked through.
Serve hot with potatoes and gravy, or cold in a roll with mustard.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the beef, pork and eggs.

recipes.curationNote: GuteKüche, Klassische Frikadellen for every amount and step; serves 4: 1 roll, 300 g pork, 300 g beef, 1 onion, 1 tbsp butter, 2 eggs, a knife tip each of paprika, salt and pepper, 3 tbsp oil, 2 tbsp parsley; same batch as ours.

recipes.name: Kasseler mit Sauerkraut
recipes.flavorProfile: Mild, smoky cured pork in juicy slices on a bed of soft, tangy sauerkraut with juniper and bay, with boiled potatoes and mustard.
recipes.healthBenefit: Kasseler gives protein and the sauerkraut brings fibre and vitamin C; the cured pork is salty, so the sauerkraut and potatoes need little more salt.

ingredients.baseName: Pork loin chop, raw cured, smoked

instructions: Soften the onion in the oil in a wide pot, 3 to 4 minutes.
Add the sauerkraut, bay leaves, juniper, peppercorns, white wine and broth and stir well.
Lay the Kasseler on top, cover and simmer gently until heated through and the sauerkraut is soft, 20 to 25 minutes for slices or 40 to 50 minutes for a whole piece.
Meanwhile boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, 20 to 25 minutes.
Slice the Kasseler and serve it on the sauerkraut with the potatoes and mustard.
recipes.curationNote: GuteKüche, Kasseler mit Sauerkraut for every amount and step; serves 4: 700 g Kasseler, 1 onion, 2 tbsp oil, 500 g sauerkraut, 3 bay leaves, 5 juniper berries, 250 ml broth; 2559 adds 6 peppercorns and a splash of dry white wine. The Kasseler is bought cured and smoked.

recipes.name: Eisbein
recipes.flavorProfile: A pink, cured pork hock simmered until the meat slips from the bone, with soft juniper sauerkraut and sharp mustard.
recipes.healthBenefit: The hock gives protein and collagen and the sauerkraut adds fibre and vitamin C; it is fatty and salty, so it is a hearty plate for a cold day.

ingredients.prepNote: bought cured (gepökelt) hock, weighed with the bone
2 litres for the hock, 500 ml for the sauerkraut
2 tbsp for the hock cooking water, poured away unless ladled into the sauerkraut
a pinch for the hock, a pinch ground for the sauerkraut
1 tsp whole for the hock, 4 more for the sauerkraut

instructions: Put the hock in a large pot with 2 litres (8.5 cups) of water, the onions, carrots, salt, caraway, peppercorns, allspice and bay leaves.
Bring to a boil, skim, then simmer gently, covered, until the meat comes away from the bone, 2 to 2.5 hours.

About 40 minutes before the end, put the sauerkraut in a second pot with the oil, juniper, 4 peppercorns, a pinch of ground caraway and 500 ml (2 cups) of water or ladles of the hock broth, and simmer, covered, 30 minutes.
For a browned rind, roast the drained hock at 430 to 465°F (220 to 240°C) for 10 to 15 minutes.
Serve the hock on the sauerkraut with mustard and boiled potatoes or Berlin pea purée.
recipes.curationNote: GuteKüche, Eisbein mit Sauerkraut for every amount and step; for 4: 1.3 kg Eisbein, 3 small onions, 3 carrots, 2 tbsp salt, a pinch of caraway, 1 tsp peppercorns, 6 allspice, 2 bay, 2 l water; sauerkraut with 500 ml water, 4 juniper, 4 peppercorns, a pinch of ground caraway, a splash of sunflower oil. The hock is bought cured. The database holds it cooked, and the bone is not taken out of the weight, so the figures for the meat run high.

recipes.name: Leberkäse
recipes.flavorProfile: A smooth, pink, finely ground pork loaf baked until a dark crust forms, eaten in thick warm slices with sweet mustard and a pretzel or roll.
recipes.healthBenefit: Leberkäse gives protein and B vitamins from the pork, but with its back fat and curing salt it is a rich, salty treat to enjoy now and then.

ingredients.cutPrep: neck or shoulder, well chilled, in cubes

instructions: Mix the chilled meat and fat with the curing salt, paprika, white pepper, chili and mace and put everything in the freezer for 20 to 30 minutes, so it stays cold while it is worked.
Grind it twice through the fine plate of a meat grinder.
Blend the ground meat in a food processor in batches with the crushed ice and grated onion to a smooth, pale, sticky paste, keeping it below 54°F (12°C).
Heat the oven to 355°F (180°C), oil a loaf tin, press in the paste without air pockets, smooth the top and score it in a diamond pattern.
Bake 15 minutes, then lower the oven to 250°F (120°C) and bake until the centre reaches 162°F (72°C), 60 to 90 minutes.
Let it rest 10 minutes and serve in thick warm slices with sweet mustard, a pretzel or roll, or potato salad.
recipes.curationNote: GuteKüche, Bayrischer Leberkäse for every amount and step; serves 4 as given; same quantities make our 8 slices.

recipes.name: Currywurst
recipes.flavorProfile: Crisp-skinned fried sausage in bite-size pieces under a warm, sweet and tangy tomato curry sauce with a final dusting of curry powder.
recipes.healthBenefit: The sausage gives protein, but the sweet ketchup sauce and fried sausage make this a street-food treat that is high in salt and sugar.

components.note: 4 tsp, 3 in the sauce, 1 to dust

instructions: Soften the onion in 1 tbsp oil over medium heat, 4 to 5 minutes, then stir in the sugar and a splash of water and let it caramelise lightly before adding the tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the honey, balsamic vinegar, ketchup, soy sauce, 3 tsp curry powder, cayenne and pepper and simmer gently, 10 to 15 minutes, then blend smooth if you like.
Fry the sausages in the remaining oil over medium heat until browned and crisp on all sides, 8 to 10 minutes.
Cut the sausages into thick slices, spoon over the hot sauce and dust with the last of the curry powder.
Serve with a roll or fries.
recipes.curationNote: GuteKüche, Currysauce für die Currywurst for every amount and step; for 6: 2 onions, 2 tbsp oil, 1 tsp brown sugar, a splash of water, 1 tsp tomato paste, 1 tbsp honey, 3 tbsp balsamic, 500 ml ketchup, a pinch each of pepper and chilli, a splash of soy, 2 tbsp curry powder; ours is half.

recipes.name: Labskaus
recipes.flavorProfile: A soft, pink mash of corned beef, potato, onion and beetroot, salty and gently sour, crowned with a fried egg and served with rollmops and gherkins.
recipes.healthBenefit: The beef and eggs give protein, iron and vitamin B12 and the potatoes and beetroot add potassium and folate; with cured beef and pickles it is a salty sailor dish.

components.note: 150 g, 70 g finely chopped, the rest to serve

ingredients.prepNote: 5 peppercorns for the pot plus a pinch ground to season
1 tsp, mostly for the water the brisket simmers in; a little of the broth goes into the mash

instructions: Simmer the brisket in the water with 1 tsp salt, the bay leaf, peppercorns and cloves until very tender, 2 to 2.5 hours. Add the quartered onions for the last 10 minutes. Lift out the meat and onions and keep a cup of the broth.
Boil the potatoes until soft, 20 to 25 minutes, and drain.
Mince or finely chop the beef and onions, then mash them with the potatoes, chopped gherkins and chopped beetroot, loosening it with a little broth and gherkin brine.
Season with the mustard, a pinch of salt and a pinch of ground pepper, and keep warm over low heat, stirring so it does not catch.
Fry the eggs sunny side up in the butter and serve each plate of Labskaus topped with an egg, with a rollmops, beetroot and gherkins beside it.
recipes.curationNote: GuteKüche, Labskaus Hamburger Art for every amount and step; serves 4, same as ours.

recipes.name: Hühnerfrikassee
recipes.flavorProfile: Tender pieces of chicken with carrots, peas, asparagus and mushrooms in a pale, creamy sauce brightened with lemon and a few capers, over rice.
recipes.healthBenefit: Chicken breast gives lean protein and niacin, and the vegetables add fibre, folate and vitamin K, with cream and yolk making the sauce rich.

ingredients.prepNote: a pinch for the sauce, a pinch for the rice

ingredients.baseName: Grains, rice, white, long-grain, regular, dry

instructions: Simmer the chicken gently in the broth until just cooked, 15 to 20 minutes, then lift it out, cut it in bite-size pieces and keep the broth.
Cook the carrots in the broth 6 to 8 minutes, the asparagus 5 to 6 minutes and the peas 2 to 3 minutes, lifting each out when tender.
Cook the rice in the water with a pinch of salt, covered, over low heat, 15 to 18 minutes.
Fry the mushrooms in the butter 3 to 4 minutes, stir in the flour and cook 1 minute, then whisk in about 600 ml (2.5 cups) of the broth and simmer 8 to 10 minutes.
Stir in the cream, return the chicken and vegetables, add the capers, and season with lemon juice, sugar, nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Take the pan off the heat, stir a ladle of sauce into the yolks and stir them back in to bind without boiling, then serve over the rice.
recipes.curationNote: GuteKüche, Hühnerfrikassee for every amount and step; serves 4: 600 g chicken breast, 1 l broth, 200 g carrots, 150 g peas, 2 tbsp butter, 3 tbsp flour, a pinch each of salt, pepper and nutmeg, a splash of lemon juice, 2 yolks, 200 ml cream; the Uckermark version (7704) adds asparagus, mushrooms, capers and a pinch of sugar.

recipes.name: Rindergulasch
recipes.flavorProfile: Tender beef in a thick, dark red sauce that is sweet with slow-cooked onion and deep with paprika, finished with a spoon of crème fraîche.
recipes.healthBenefit: The beef gives protein, iron, zinc and vitamin B12, and the onions, tomatoes and paprika add vitamin C, which helps the iron along.
instructions: Brown the beef in the hot Butterschmalz in batches over high heat, 3 to 4 minutes a batch, and set aside.
Fry the onions in the same pot over medium heat until soft and golden, 10 to 15 minutes, stirring in the sugar toward the end.
Add the garlic and tomato paste and cook 1 minute, then take the pot off the heat and stir in the paprika so it does not turn bitter.
Return the beef with the tomatoes, broth and mustard, cover and braise over low heat until tender, 1.5 to 2 hours, stirring now and then.
Season with salt and pepper, stir in the crème fraîche, and serve with Spätzle, noodles, potatoes or bread dumplings.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the tomatoes, onions and paprika.

recipes.curationNote: GuteKüche, Rindergulasch for every amount and step; its 4 portions use the same quantities as our 6.

recipes.name: Kohlrouladen
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, sweet cabbage leaves wrapped around a peppery mince and rice filling, browned and braised in a tomato and mustard sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: Cabbage gives fibre and vitamins C and K and the mince gives protein, iron and vitamin B12, making a well-rounded one-pan plate.

ingredients.baseName: Grains, rice, white, long-grain, regular, dry

ingredients.prepNote: a pinch for the filling, a pinch for the braise
a pinch for the filling, a pinch for the braise

instructions: Cut out the core and blanch the cabbage whole in boiling salted water, peeling off the outer leaves as they soften, 2 to 3 minutes each, until you have 16. Shave down the thick rib of each leaf.
Parboil the rice for 10 minutes and drain. Soften the onions in 1 tbsp oil, 4 to 5 minutes.
Mix the minces with the rice, half the onions, the mustard, paprika, salt and pepper.
Lay two leaves overlapping, put an eighth of the filling on them, fold in the sides and roll up tightly. Tie with kitchen string.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Brown the rolls on all sides in the remaining oil in an ovenproof pan, 6 to 8 minutes.

Add the rest of the onions and the tomato paste, cook 1 minute, pour in the broth, season with a pinch each of salt and pepper, cover and bake until the cabbage is soft, 30 to 40 minutes, basting once. Serve with boiled potatoes and the sauce.
recipes.curationNote: GuteKüche, Kohlrouladen for every amount and step; serves 4: 1 kg cabbage, 5 tbsp oil, 250 ml stock, 100 g rice, 4 onions, 3 tbsp tomato paste, 700 g mixed mince, 3 tbsp hot mustard, 0.5 tsp sweet paprika, a pinch each of salt and pepper in the filling and in the braise, plus 1 tsp salt in the rice water that is drained.

recipes.name: Falscher Hase
recipes.flavorProfile: A juicy, herby meatloaf with a whole row of hard-boiled eggs hidden inside, sliced thick and served in a creamy sour cream gravy.
recipes.healthBenefit: The meat and eggs give protein, iron and vitamin B12 in generous amounts, and the root vegetables in the pan add a little fibre to the gravy.

ingredients.prepNote: 1 tsp for the meat, a pinch for the gravy
0.5 tsp for the meat, a pinch for the gravy

instructions: Heat the oven to 355°F (180°C) fan, or 390°F (200°C) without fan.
Mix the minces with the breadcrumbs, onion, garlic, parsley, thyme, marjoram, paprika, mustard, raw eggs, salt and pepper.
Shape half the mixture into a long flat loaf in a roasting pan, lay the boiled eggs end to end down the middle, cover with the rest and press the loaf closed and smooth.
Scatter the root vegetables around it, pour in half the broth and roast until browned and cooked through, about 1 hour, adding more broth as it reduces.
Lift out the loaf and rest it 10 minutes, strain or blend the pan juices with the vegetables, and stir in the sour cream with a pinch each of salt and pepper to make the gravy.
Slice so each piece shows a ring of egg and serve with mashed potatoes and the gravy.

recipes.name: Zwiebelrostbraten
recipes.flavorProfile: Seared beef steaks with a mustard edge under a heap of crisp, sweet fried onions and a dark red wine gravy.
recipes.healthBenefit: The beef gives protein, iron, zinc and vitamin B12, and the onions add a little fibre; the fried onion makes it a rich Sunday plate.

ingredients.cutPrep: 3 for the steaks, 1 for the onions
1 to dust the onions, 1 for the gravy

instructions: Season the steaks with salt and pepper and brush one side with mustard.
Sear them in 3 tbsp hot oil over high heat, 1 to 2 minutes a side, and set aside.
Dust half the onion rings with flour and fry them in the drippings with the remaining oil until crisp and brown, 8 to 10 minutes, then lift them onto paper.
Fry the rest of the onions in the pan until soft and golden, 6 to 8 minutes, stir in the remaining flour, then deglaze with the red wine and broth.
Return the steaks, cover and braise over low heat until tender, 45 minutes to 1 hour, then simmer the gravy uncovered until it coats a spoon.
Serve the steaks in the gravy, piled with the crisp onions, with Spätzle or fried potatoes.
recipes.curationNote: GuteKüche, Zwiebelrostbraten for every amount and step; serves 4, same as ours; its packaged sauce powder is replaced by flour, as ours already did.

recipes.name: Strammer Max
recipes.flavorProfile: Buttered dark bread with salty ham and mild melting cheese under a soft fried egg, the yolk running into the bread.
recipes.healthBenefit: Eggs, ham and cheese give protein, vitamin B12 and calcium and the rye bread adds fibre; the cured ham makes it salty, so it is a hearty snack rather than an everyday lunch.
instructions: Butter the bread and toast it lightly, buttered side down, in a pan over medium heat, 1 to 2 minutes.
Lay two slices of ham and a slice of Gouda on each piece of bread and warm them under a lid or in a 355°F (180°C) oven until the cheese softens, 3 to 5 minutes.
Meanwhile fry the eggs sunny side up in the oil over medium heat, 3 to 4 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks still soft.
Slide an egg onto each bread, season with salt and pepper and scatter with chives and parsley.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the eggs, ham and cheese.
From the eggs, ham and cheese.

recipes.curationNote: GuteKüche, Strammer Max for every amount and step; 4 bread slices and 4 eggs, the same quantities ours uses.

recipes.name: Senfeier
recipes.flavorProfile: Halved soft-set eggs in a smooth, tangy mustard sauce with a hint of nutmeg, over boiled potatoes with fresh herbs.
recipes.healthBenefit: The eggs give protein, vitamin B12 and choline and the potatoes add potassium and vitamin C, for a thrifty vegetarian plate.
instructions: Boil the potatoes in water with 1 tsp salt until tender, 20 to 25 minutes, and drain.
Boil the eggs 8 to 9 minutes, cool them in cold water, peel and halve them.
Soften the onion in the butter, 3 minutes, stir in the flour and cook 1 to 2 minutes without browning.
Whisk in the hot broth a little at a time and simmer, stirring, until smooth and thick, 8 to 10 minutes.
Stir in the cream and mustard, and season with sugar, nutmeg, salt and pepper; do not let it boil again once the mustard is in.
Warm the eggs in the sauce for 2 to 3 minutes and serve over the potatoes with parsley and chives.
recipes.curationNote: GuteKüche, Senfeier for every amount and step; serves 5, scaled to our 4; cream, sugar and herbs from GuteKüche 8209 (serves 2, doubled).

recipes.name: Matjes nach Hausfrauenart
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, mild Matjes herring in a cool, creamy sauce that is gently sweet and sour, with crisp apple, sharp onion and dill.
recipes.healthBenefit: Herring is one of the richest sources of omega-3 fats and vitamin D, and the apple and onion add freshness; the cream makes it rich and the cured fish is salty.
instructions: Rinse the Matjes fillets, pat them dry and cut them into bite-size pieces.
Toss the diced apple with the lemon juice so it stays pale, and separate the onion rings.
Whisk the cream and sour cream with the mustard, vinegar, sugar, curry powder, salt and pepper into a smooth, sweet and sour sauce.
Fold in the apple, onion and most of the dill, then pour it over the herring in a dish.
Cover and chill at least 30 minutes, or up to overnight for the fullest flavor, and serve scattered with the rest of the dill, with hot jacket potatoes or boiled potatoes.
recipes.curationNote: GuteKüche, Matjes nach Hausfrauenart for every amount and step; serves 4, same as ours; sour cream, lemon and dill from GuteKüche 5722. The Matjes are bought.

recipes.name: Bismarckhering
recipes.flavorProfile: Firm, bright herring fillets pickled in a sharp, spiced vinegar brine with soft onion rings, bay and mustard seed.
recipes.healthBenefit: Herring brings omega-3 fats, vitamin D and vitamin B12, and pickling keeps them; the cure is salty, so a fillet or two is a good portion.

ingredients.cutPrep: from 4 fresh herrings, heads, bones and guts removed
4 for the cure, 1 for the brine
ingredients.prepNote: part for the cure, which is rinsed off, part for the brine; about half stays in the fish

instructions: For safety with raw fish, freeze the cleaned fillets at -4°F (-20°C) for at least 24 hours, then thaw them in the fridge.
Rub the fillets thickly with 4 tsp salt, cover and leave them in the fridge for 3 to 4 hours, then rinse and pat dry.
Bring the onions, vinegar, water, lemon slices, bay leaves, mustard seed, peppercorns, juniper, sugar and 1 tsp salt to a boil and boil 3 minutes, then let the brine cool completely.
Layer the fillets in a clean jar or dish with the onions and lemon and pour over the cold brine so they are covered.
Close and keep in the fridge for 3 days before eating, and eat within 1 to 2 weeks. Serve with boiled or fried potatoes, or in a roll.
recipes.curationNote: GuteKüche, Bismarckhering mit Salzkartoffeln for every amount and step; 4 herrings, 4 tsp salt for the cure; brine of 4 onions, 500 ml white wine vinegar, 500 ml water, 1 lemon, 2 bay leaves, 0.5 tsp mustard seed, 5 peppercorns, 5 juniper berries, 1 tsp sugar, 1 tsp salt; same amounts as ours.

recipes.name: Rollmops
recipes.flavorProfile: Pickled herring rolled around a crisp strip of gherkin and onion, tart, salty and refreshing.
recipes.healthBenefit: Herring brings omega-3 fats, vitamin D and vitamin B12; the pickling brine makes it salty, so it is a small bite rather than a meal.

components.note: all 8 fillets, drained, the brine kept

instructions: Lay the drained Bismarck fillets skin side down and spread each thinly with mustard if you like.
Lay a strip of gherkin and a few strips of red onion across the wide end of each fillet.
Roll each fillet up tightly from the wide end and pin it closed with one or two toothpicks.
Pack the rolls into a jar with the bay leaves and mustard seed, pour the saved brine over them so they are covered, close and chill.
Let them rest in the fridge 2 days before eating, and eat within 1 week. Serve with brown bread or as part of Labskaus.
recipes.curationNote: Built on the Bismarckhering recipe, as GuteKüche 20902 does with jarred Bismarck herrings rolled with bay and onion and returned to their brine for 2 days. GuteKüche 28771 and Wikibooks gave the gherkin and onion filling. The mustard is a common addition and kept optional.

recipes.name: Forelle Müllerin Art
recipes.flavorProfile: Whole trout dusted in flour and fried golden, with tender, sweet flesh, lemon and nutty butter poured over with fresh herbs.
recipes.healthBenefit: Trout gives lean protein, omega-3 fats, vitamin D and vitamin B12, cooked simply with a modest amount of butter.
instructions: Rinse the trout and pat them dry, drizzle inside and out with lemon juice and season with salt and pepper, tucking some of the parsley, chives and lemon balm inside.
Heat the oven to 355°F (180°C). Turn the trout in flour and shake off the extra.
Fry them in the hot Butterschmalz over medium heat until golden and crisp, 4 to 5 minutes a side.
Move the trout to a baking tray, dot each with a little of the butter and finish in the oven, 8 to 10 minutes, until the flesh lifts from the bone.
Brown the rest of the butter in the pan until it smells nutty, 1 to 2 minutes, stir in the remaining parsley and chives and pour it over the fish. Serve with lemon wedges and boiled parsley potatoes.

citations.source: GuteKüche, Forelle nach Art der Müllerin

recipes.curationNote: GuteKüche, Forelle nach Art der Müllerin for every amount and step; serves 2: 2 trout, juice of 1 lemon, 50 g flour, 2 tbsp Butterschmalz, 4 tsp butter, 1/2 bunch parsley, 1/2 bunch chives, 1 sprig lemon balm, a pinch each of salt and pepper; doubled for our 4.

recipes.name: Backfisch
recipes.flavorProfile: Flaky white fish in a light, crisp, golden beer batter, seasoned with mustard and lemon, served hot with potato salad.
recipes.healthBenefit: Redfish gives lean protein, vitamin B12 and selenium; frying in batter makes it richer, so a vegetable side helps balance the plate.

ingredients.cutPrep: for the batter, plus a little for dusting
the amount the fish takes up from the frying oil

instructions: Season the fish with salt, pepper and lemon juice, brush it thinly with mustard and leave it 10 minutes.
Whisk the flour, starch, cold beer, egg yolk, sugar and a pinch of salt into a smooth, thick batter and rest it 15 minutes, then fold in the egg white beaten to soft peaks.
Heat rapeseed oil about 2 inches (5 cm) deep to 340°F (170°C).
Pat the fish dry, dust it with flour, dip it in the batter and let the extra drip off.
Fry 2 or 3 pieces at a time until puffed and golden, 4 to 5 minutes, turning once, and drain on a rack.
Serve at once with lemon and potato salad or remoulade.
recipes.curationNote: GuteKüche, Backfisch auf Kartoffelsalat for every amount and step; serves 4 like ours; mustard, lemon and sugar from GuteKüche 5650 (serves 3).

recipes.name: Scholle Finkenwerder Art
recipes.flavorProfile: Whole plaice fried golden in butter, sweet and delicate, under a shower of crisp smoky bacon, onion and parsley with lemon.
recipes.healthBenefit: Plaice gives lean protein, vitamin B12 and iodine; the bacon adds flavour and some salt and fat.

ingredients.cutPrep: 4 whole plaice of about 400 g, cleaned, rinsed and dusted with flour

ingredients.prepNote: juice of 1 lemon; 1 more lemon in wedges to serve is not counted

instructions: Drizzle the plaice with the juice of one lemon and leave 10 minutes, then pat dry, season inside and out with salt and white pepper and turn in flour.
Heat the oven to 175°F (80°C) to keep the fish warm.
Fry the bacon in a dry pan until crisp and golden, 8 to 10 minutes, add the onion for the last 3 to 4 minutes, then lift both out and keep warm.
Fry the plaice one or two at a time in the Butterschmalz and bacon fat, dark side down first, 4 to 5 minutes a side, and keep each warm in the oven.
Scatter the fish with the bacon, onion and parsley and serve with lemon wedges and potato salad or boiled potatoes.

citations.source: GuteKüche, Gebratene Scholle nach Finkenwerder Art

recipes.curationNote: GuteKüche, Finkenwerder Scholle for every amount and step; serves 4, same as ours; onion and white pepper as in GuteKüche 16476.

recipes.name: Fischfrikadellen
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, juicy fish cakes with sweet onion, lots of parsley and a little North Sea shrimp, fried until crisp and golden.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pollock, redfish and shrimp give lean protein, vitamin B12, selenium and iodine in an easy, family-friendly form.

components.note: 3 each, stale, soaked in 125 ml water and squeezed

ingredients.cutPrep: small North Sea shrimp, peeled, chopped

instructions: Sweat the onion in the oil over low heat until soft, 8 to 10 minutes, and let it cool.
Chop the fish finely with a knife or pulse it briefly in a processor, keeping some texture.
Mix the fish with the shrimp, squeezed rolls, onion, egg, parsley, nutmeg, curry, salt and pepper, and add breadcrumbs until the mixture holds its shape.
Shape 8 flat cakes with wet hands and chill them 15 to 20 minutes.
Fry in the hot Butterschmalz over medium heat until golden and cooked through, 5 to 6 minutes a side.
Serve with lemon, potato salad or a remoulade.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the sea fish and shrimp.

recipes.name: Hamburger Pannfisch
recipes.flavorProfile: Golden pan-fried pieces of cod and redfish over crisp fried potatoes, with a creamy, tangy mustard sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: Cod and redfish give lean protein, vitamin B12, selenium and iodine, and the potatoes add potassium; the cream sauce and fried potatoes make it a hearty plate.

ingredients.cutPrep: 2 for the fish, 1 for the sauce

ingredients.prepNote: a pinch each for the potatoes, fish and sauce
a pinch each for the fish and sauce

ingredients.cutPrep: waxy, boiled in their skins the day before, peeled and sliced
1 in thin strips for the potatoes, 1 diced for the sauce
1 tbsp for the sauce onion, the rest cold to finish

instructions: Fry the potato slices in the oil in a wide pan over medium heat, turning now and then, until golden and crisp, 15 to 20 minutes, adding the onion strips for the last 5 minutes and seasoning with a pinch of salt.
For the sauce, soften the diced onion in 1 tbsp butter, 3 minutes, stir in 1 tbsp flour, whisk in the broth and simmer 5 minutes.
Stir in the cream, mustard, sugar, 2 tsp lemon juice and a pinch each of salt and pepper, take it off the heat and swirl in the cold butter. Do not boil it again.
Drizzle the fish with lemon juice, season with a pinch each of salt and pepper and dust with flour.
Fry the fish in the hot Butterschmalz 2 to 3 minutes a side, until golden and just flaking.
Lay the fish over the fried potatoes in the pan and serve with the mustard sauce beside it.

recipes.name: Heringssalat
recipes.flavorProfile: Tender pieces of Matjes herring with crisp apple, gherkin and onion in a cool, sweet and sour cream dressing with chives.
recipes.healthBenefit: Herring brings omega-3 fats, vitamin D and vitamin B12 and the apple adds fibre; the cream dressing makes it rich, so a small bowl goes a long way.
instructions: Cut the Matjes fillets into small pieces, about 0.5 inch (1 cm).
Dice the apples and mix them with the onions and gherkins.
Season the cream with the vinegar and sugar until it is gently sweet and sour, stir in the oil, and season with salt and pepper.
Fold the herring, apple, onion and gherkin into the dressing.
Cover and chill at least 2 hours so the flavors settle, and serve scattered with chives, with jacket potatoes or dark bread.
recipes.curationNote: GuteKüche, Heringssalat for every amount and step; serves 4: 6 Matjes, 3 apples, 4 gherkins, 3 onions, 2 tbsp chives, 500 ml cream, a splash each of oil and white wine vinegar, a pinch each of sugar, salt and pepper. The Matjes are bought.
